title: Research: sharp COPY71 on the remaining A8 simplex P112 frame orbit (no new kappa)
body:
## Change and mathematical scope

PR #1304 leaves the fixed A8 simplex decoder on nonmatching P112 frame punctures open. This proves the sharp separate COPY cost **71** for the complementary **1,080 frames**, over arbitrary complex per-row kernel shifts. An all-nine-active exact witness attains the bound. The frame census partitions all 2,025 E8 eight-frames into the predecessor's 945 matching frames and these 1,080 frames, each consisting of one pair root and a Fano plane on the remaining coordinates.

This is a scoped proof with exhaustive finite lemmas, not a supplier or κ improvement. The nine simplex normals are fixed, exactness is on all live pairs with ordinary transpose, and terms are billed separately. The COPY power bill also exceeds the eight rank-eight coordinate terms for `0<=a<1`, **when width, normalization and multiplicity are fixed**. No full supplier invoice is claimed. Only `research/a8-one-pair-frame-floor/` is added; no pending theorem is assumed for its bound.

## Task and overlap

- Task `complex-masked-decoder`, scope **refined** to PR #1304's explicit other-frame question; [task and overlap record](https://github.com/bbMisk/integer-mult-bounds/blob/da6308454686c77372e82a60e196ccb828285360/research/a8-one-pair-frame-floor/TASK.json).
- Research base: `ebedc0895eb4c06725af020bc1af165722b0a3ce` (priority revision 2); submission rebased onto `81e81af67714bdc8d1693b0bf5c29468b92f62ff`. Revision 3 was read and this completed COPY obstruction retained; it is not a new packing/κ claim.
- Contribution head: `da6308454686c77372e82a60e196ccb828285360`.
- Predecessors: #1304 `a052f0da36a3845c2ec785fd44e5b9e50de3b688`; #1248 `f226f4329a996b0a1bea8794179a91b5d0ed80bf`; #1224 `00e6ed0810b8ebc7f6133e2c036d0f1c9a3a4162`. Their heads were rechecked. Source file blobs and hashes are pinned.
- [Scoped claim](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1241#discussioncomment-18914233). Submission overlap covered 733 open PRs and 244 discussion records with complete pagination at 03:52 UTC on October 14. No competing result for this orbit was found within that coverage; no novelty guarantee.

## Validation

```sh
python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/a8-one-pair-frame-floor
```

Passed on macOS arm64 / CPython 3.12.13. The primary checks all nine anchors: **390,915 binary planes, 20,019 partner-space tuples and 382,032 compatible choices**. Two sharp witnesses have costs `(0,8,9,9,9,9,9,9,9)` and `(1,8,8,9,9,9,9,9,9)`; both all-pairs identities are checked exactly. The [written proof](https://github.com/bbMisk/integer-mult-bounds/blob/da6308454686c77372e82a60e196ccb828285360/research/a8-one-pair-frame-floor/PROOF.md) explains why the finite compatibility cover bounds every complex shift.

The second arithmetic implementation uses Gram-derived labels, nullspaces, Cartesian products and verified stabilizer transport. A separate pair/Fano construction agrees with the full frame census. Both implementations are explicitly credited adaptations of #1304; this is not independent peer review.

Ten semantic controls and all five package test groups pass, including false/missing/malformed receipts, incomplete anchor coverage, changed frame coverage, optimized execution and read-only relocation. Both mathematical checkers also pass under optimized CPython 3.14.6. The prescribed predecessor positive control, selected-result integrity check and metadata/source pins pass.

Not checked: physical gathering, frames, restoration, hosting, precision/tape, all-size/compiler, common-label/mutable-source, analytic and bit H1–H5 obligations. No selected cold replay, Lean, hosted-CI success, human review or maintainer acceptance is claimed.

Credit the retained DreamingOfClouds (#717/#595/#446), Joel Pulikkan/GamingPuzzled (#620), themilkman216 (#968) and woklerx (#1077) lineage. Exact original file pins and adaptation notices are retained. Apache-2.0.

Prepared for Hanson Sun (@bbMisk), with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance in the mathematics, implementations, verification and writing.

## Open next questions

[Structured questions and limits](https://github.com/bbMisk/integer-mult-bounds/blob/da6308454686c77372e82a60e196ccb828285360/research/a8-one-pair-frame-floor/README.md#open-next-questions): a different specified nine-normal family, starting with its kernel-shift and column-rank calculation; or a physical shared-copy contract with a complete bill. The fixed simplex and separate-term assumptions block transferring this theorem to those cases.
